## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design cross-platform bridges, handle asynchronous permission flows, UX when denied, and keeping state consistent across RN and OS.

## Key Concepts

- Cross-platform RN bridges (RCTBridgeModule) in Swift and Kotlin
- Unified permission model and statuses
- UX for denied/blocked permissions and settings redirection
- Caching results and avoiding redundant prompts

## Code Example

```javascript
import { NativeModules, NativeEventEmitter } from 'react-native';
const { RNPermissions } = NativeModules;
const emitter = new NativeEventEmitter(RNPermissions);
RNPermissions.checkPermissions(['camera','microphone','storage']).then(set => { /* ... */ });
RNPermissions.requestPermissions(['camera']).then(res => { /* ... */ });
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How to handle permission changes when app moves to background?
- How to test mocked permission flows in CI?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical React Native bridge profiling skills—the ability to design actionable per-frame metrics with minimal overhead and privacy-conscious JS-Native communication.

## Key Concepts
- Frame timing architecture: leveraging CADisplayLink (iOS) and Choreographer (Android) for accurate per-frame callbacks
- Rolling ring buffer: fixed 1024-sample window to prevent unbounded memory growth and minimize GC pressure
- Sampling overhead: target 16ms intervals (60fps) with minimal CPU impact
- Privacy: opt-in profiling with on-device aggregation, no PII collection

## Code Example
```javascript
import { NativePerfModule } from 'react-native';

NativePerfModule.startProfile({ sampleMs: 16 });
const metrics = await NativePerfModule.getMetrics();
```

## Why This Is Asked

This question probes cross-thread orchestration, efficient media pipelines, and JS-Native bridge design at scale. It requires concrete API, backpressure strategy, and real-world trade-offs.

## Key Concepts

- TurboModules and JSI bridging
- Dedicated native threads for I/O and ML, with a bounded queue
- Backpressure and frame-dropping policies
- Buffer reuse and zero-copy techniques
- Power and memory management on mobile hardware

## Code Example
